uncited: *   **Ring Buffer Management:** A technique for maintaining a fixed-size window of data items to ensure the most relevant time slices are always available for interpolation.
It differs from simple FIFO queues by allowing circular reuse of memory slots.
Choose this when memory is constrained but continuous access to a sliding window of time steps is required.
*   **Asynchronous CUDA Streams:** A mechanism for overlapping data transfer with computation.
It differs from synchronous transfers by allowing the CPU to continue scheduling tasks while the GPU processes previous ones.

*   **When not to use:** When the entire dataset fits in GPU memory (uploading all is simpler and faster); when network bandwidth is the bottleneck in a distributed setting (see [Distributed computing and load balancing](5624-distributed-computing-and-load-balancing.md)).
